idiom_name: state holder plus a func(State) render callback; html/template for server-rendered markup
implementation_notes: Go has first-class function values, so the mechanism is a plain parameter of function type - func(state State) string or func(w io.Writer, s State) - and the owner simply calls it whenever its state changes; the full structure (state holder, callback field, invocation points) is hand-written around that parameter because no component runtime exists. The conventional rendering path in Go is html/template, where the caller supplies a template rather than a function; use the callback form when the rendering decision must be code (immediate-mode GUI layers, programmatic emitters) and the template form when the markup is data-driven. There is no framework-supplied component whose props are templates, so keep the plumbing small and explicit.
pitfalls: A nil function value panics when called; owners should reject nil callbacks at construction or document that the render function is required.
Calling the render function from a goroutine while the caller mutates shared state races; invoke it synchronously or pass the state by value and let the consumer synchronize.
Closures capture loop variables unless the values are passed as parameters - the classic Go aliasing bug when the owner fires callbacks from a loop.
